title: an `_arguments` action command word that is a builtin or an external program is run (zsh); zshrs ran neither and printed nothing — `r` via sh:465's scalar first character, `uname` as a bare action

observed.measured: 2026-10-30, target/debug/zshrs with the dispatch_action_command builtin arm (zshrs 0.13.56) vs zsh 5.9.999.3-test (~/.cache/zshrs/zsh-oracle-new), scripts/compsys_spec_fuzz.py --spec
observed.notes: The message `pat*` ends at the first colon, so the action is `rest:(r1 r2)`. sh:463 `eval "action=( $action )"` fails (`unknown file attribute: 1`), `action` stays a scalar, and sh:465 runs `"$action[1]"` = `r`, the `fc -e -` builtin, with `$expl` (`-J ...`). Src/exec.c runs a builtin in the current shell through execbuiltin; dispatch_action_command returned 1 for every builtin without running it. The variant pins the `$PATH` arm: `uname` is forked and exec'd with `$expl`, and its own `illegal option -- J` diagnostic lands after the command line.

observed_when_diverging.recorded_under: target/debug/zshrs at a9add374ed before the fix (zshrs 0.13.56) vs zsh 5.9.999.3-test

why_this_fixture_exists: Found by the round-2 lane-1 `_arguments` probe `*:pat*:rest:(r1 r2)`. Any builtin reached as an action command word (sh:455 / sh:465, `_all_labels` sh:35 / sh:39) was silently treated as a failed action.

variants.note: WHEN THIS DIVERGED: zsh row 0 `@SFZ@ fzc0000 uname: illegal option -- J`, row 1 `usage: uname [-amnoprsv]`; zshrs printed nothing (dispatch_action_command answered 1 for any `$PATH` executable). Src/exec.c:4369 execute() forks and execs it.
